claim: Does the caller's name survive transcription? (recording of 2026-08-08)
_provenance: 37s of a Nigerian caller on a live Twilio line, inbound track only, mu-law 8kHz.
The audio is gitignored and stays that way: it is a person saying their own name and
an identifier aloud. This file holds the transcript side and no audio, which is why
The name is recorded in docs/STACK_DECISION.md (2026-08-08, third run) and in TASKS.md.
Six runs out of six — both encodings, harness and production adapter — returned
"Chike". That is the thing this claim is here to keep measurable.

unlabelled.reason: the caller reads a policy number on this recording and the digits were never written down. Deriving them from a transcriber's output would seed ground truth from a candidate, which R9.1.4 forbids. Someone has to listen to the audio and write down what was said.
no hand transcript of the call exists, so there is nothing to compute WER against. Prose scoring is deferred with the rest of Gate A — see README.md.

_configurations_note: These describe the four runs tools/stt-compare/compare.mjs performs and are filled in
from that file and from .env as of 2026-08-09. CHECK THEM AGAINST YOUR OWN .env BEFORE
TRUSTING A RUN — the tool reads TRANSCRIPTION_MODEL, DEEPGRAM_MODEL,
DEEPGRAM_EOT_THRESHOLD and DEEPGRAM_EOT_TIMEOUT_MS at run time and prints none of them,
so this file is the only record that the numbers had a configuration at all.
Blank out any field you have not verified: a missing field is refused, which is the
correct outcome for a result nobody can reproduce.
